'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2023 Ain al-Hilweh clashes]]
**A [[ceasefire]] is signed between [[Fatah]] and [[Islamist]] groups after three days of clashes in the [[Ain al-Hilweh]] [[Palestinian refugee camps|Palestinian refugee camp]] in [[Sidon District]], [[Lebanon]], which killed five people and injured 52 others. [https://apnews.com/article/lebanon-palestinians-refugees-clashes-camps-8f342f0a717ad01de57ec3340c9fd625 (AP)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***At least 43 people are killed and dozens more are injured by an [[airstrike]] in [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-war-military-khartoum-ded192c55c6b0e8cc29b1b5bc5965fc9 (AP)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|Crimea attacks]]
***Russia says its [[air defence]] shot down three [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]] over [[Crimea]], one in the northwest and two in the west of the [[peninsula]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-shoots-down-three-drones-crimea-says-russia-installed-official-2023-09-09/ (Reuters)]
**Two foreign [[aid worker]]s are killed and two others are injured by [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[shell (projectile)|shelling]] near [[Chasiv Yar]], [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-volunteers-killed-a8d300ce02127880ff168d610b312c6a (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 28 people are killed during a boat accident in [[Mokwa]], [[Niger State]], [[Nigeria]]. The boat carrying more than 100 passengers, mostly women and children, [[capsize]]d along the [[Niger River]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/9/11/nigeria-boat-accident-death-toll-rises-as-dozens-remain-missing (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Malagasy presidential election]]
**[[President of Madagascar|Madagascar President]] [[Andry Rajoelina]] resigns in order to run for re-election, in accordance with [[Madagascar|the country]]'s [[Constitution of Madagascar|constitution]]. Rajoelina sent his resignation letter to the High Constitutional Court following confirmation of his candidature. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/madagascar-president-resigns-ahead-polls-november-2023-09-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Censorship by Facebook]]
**[[Meta Platforms|Meta]] deletes [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] [[Arabic]] presenter Tamer Almisshal's [[Facebook]] profile a day after a programme aired an investigation into Meta’s [[censorship]] of [[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] content. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/9/10/meta-deletes-al-jazeera-presenters-profile-after-show-criticising-israel (Al Jazeera)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]
**[[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]] wins its first [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]], beating [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]] 83–77 in the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup final|final]]. [[Dennis Schröder]] is named the tournament's [[FIBA Basketball World Cup Most Valuable Player|Most Valuable Player]]. [https://apnews.com/article/basketball-world-cup-serbia-germany-final-05c2c8ed8c0478283d1cec3213002204 (AP)]
**[[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada]] earns its first medal at the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and its first medal at a global men's [[basketball]] tournament since 1936, after defeating the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] 127–118 after [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] in the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup final round#Third place game|bronze medal game]]. [https://apnews.com/article/basketball-world-cup-bronze-usa-canada-6c53d0f4a8e08d8f9b19e3bcba36c752 (AP)]
*[[Rubiales affair]]
**[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] president [[Luis Rubiales]] announces his [[resignation]] after having acted inappropriately during the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup final]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230910-luis-rubiales-from-union-boss-to-spain-s-football-federation-chief (AFP via France 24)]
